s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of multiple asymptomatic skin nodules with gradual increase in size and number
salient_findings: Multiple skin-colored nodules over neck, trunk, and upper limbs
Discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules without overlying erythema or tenderness
Single firm nodule on the lateral tongue
key_facts: 55-year-old man
Asymptomatic skin nodules for 1 year
No systemic complaints, including no fever, weight loss, or neurologic symptoms
Eats beef, denies consumption of pork
No passage of tape-like worms in stool
Normal vital signs
Unremarkable general and systemic examinations
No lymphadenopathy
Normal complete blood count and metabolic profile
Nonreactive serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C viruses

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple asymptomatic skin nodules and a nodule on the lateral tongue are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Multiple lipomas
shortlist.why_kept: Discrete, firm, freely mobile nodules without overlying erythema or tenderness are characteristic of lipomas

shortlist.label: Dermatofibromas
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic skin nodules with gradual increase in size and number could be consistent with dermatofibromas

shortlist.label: Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, non-tender nodules could be indicative of fibromatosis, a condition characterized by benign fibrous tumors

shortlist.label: Lipoid proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of asymptomatic skin nodules and a nodule on the tongue could be consistent with lipoid proteinosis, a rare condition characterized by deposits of hyaline material in the skin and other tissues

raw.rationale: The patient presents with multiple asymptomatic, skin-colored nodules that are discrete, firm, and freely mobile, which is consistent with the characteristics of lipomas. The absence of systemic complaints, normal laboratory investigations, and unremarkable general and systemic examinations also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
rejected.why: Typically associated with neurologic symptoms, cafe-au-lait spots, and other systemic features, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Dermatofibromas
rejected.why: Usually presents with a single or few lesions, often with a history of trauma, and may have overlying erythema or tenderness, which is not consistent with this patient's presentation

rejected.label: Fibromatosis
rejected.why: Often associated with larger, more aggressive lesions and may have systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Lipoid proteinosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with a broader range of systemic symptoms, including hoarseness, and skin lesions that are often more widespread and accompanied by other features such as beaded papules on the margins of the eyelids, which are not described in this case
